articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 8
articles.excerpt: Ce dimanche 8 novembre, une semaine après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, Tom Laperche a remporté l’épreuve en Ultim en établissant un nouveau record. Derrière lui, les derniers Ultim approchent des Antilles dans une atmosphère encore instable, tandis que les Ocean Fifty et les premiers IMOCA traversent la dépression tropicale. Plus à l’est, les Class40 restent au cœur du suspense.

articles.title: « I was in a state of grace »
articles.excerpt: Silhouette déliée, polo blanc, visage glabre, regard bleu profond, Tom Laperche est sorti de la nuit comme une apparition, devant un Mémorial Act comble et un ponton officiel prêt à couler. Tout le monde voulait en être ce soir pour partager les premiers moments de terrien du nouveau prince des océans qui n’a pas boudé son plaisir en revenant longuement sur son épopée victorieuse.

articles.title: Tom Laperche, from childhood dream to Route du Rhum winner
articles.excerpt: At 29, the Route du Rhum winning skipper of SVR-Lazartigue has shown talent, dedication and an acute attention to detail since a very young age.  Today  in Guadeloupe he joins the list of ocean racing greats who have won the classic solo ocean sprint. It is the most prestigious victory of his young career, an incredible triumph for a sailor for whom the legenday solo race has been a goal since he was very young.

articles.title: Tom Laperche (SVR-Lazartigue) is the winner!*
articles.excerpt: FLASH FINISH. SVR-Lazartigue crossed the finish line of the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe this Sunday at 10:31:40 PM (local time), 3:31:40 AM (Paris time). Tom Laperche achieved an incredible feat, taking the lead at Cap Fréhel and maintaining it to the finish. He completed the race in 6 days, 13 hours, 27 minutes, and 40 seconds, thus setting a new record for the most prestigious ocean sprint. He is the third skipper under 30 to win the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe, after...

articles.title: The Laperche route to victory
articles.excerpt: On a well-seasoned trimaran that he knows like the back of his hand, Tom Laperche was fast in all conditions, agile in his transitions, and sharp and commanding right from the start of the race. When confidence is combined with talent and hard work, the result is unstoppable. Way to go, maestro!

articles.title: Victory calling, course record likely
articles.excerpt: Tom Laperche (SVR) is today closing in on an historic victory on the 13th edition of the Route du Rhum-Destination Guadeloupe solo ocean sprint across the Atlantic from Saint Malo to Guadeloupe. The 29 year old was tacking upwind this morning with less than 80 miles to the Tête à l’Anglais, the little volcanic islet off the north of Basse Terre where he will turn for the climb to the finish line off Pointe-à-Pitre.

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 7
articles.excerpt: Ce samedi 7 novembre, six jours après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, Tom Laperche aborde les dernières centaines de milles vers Pointe-à- Pitre, dans un vent de sud faible et irrégulier, propice aux orages. Plus à l’est, les Class40 affrontent des conditions très contrastées autour de la dépression des Açores, avant l’arrivée d’un nouveau système perturbé en début de semaine.

articles.title: Guadeloupe waits for Laperche arrival. For others the rodeo is endless.
articles.excerpt:
Tom Laperche (SVR-Lazartigue) is expected to reach Guadeloupe sometime in the middle of the coming night (French time). He was racing upwind in a gusty SW’ly wind this morning still making 23-25kts.



A low-pressure system near the Azores continues to affect the vast majority of the solo skippers. With unstable winds, punishing seas, exhaustion, and equipment damage, there is no respite in sight.

articles.title: Black Friday for ITALIAN DUO, golden Saturday awaits Laperche
articles.excerpt: With a little over 500 nautical miles to run to the finish line off Pointe-à-Pitre and a lead of nearly 400 miles over second placed Thomas Coville (Sodebo Ultim 3), victory in the 13th edition of the 35420 nautical miles solo ocean sprint, the Route du Rhum-Destination Guadeloupe, seems all  but assured for Tom Laperche, (SVR Lazartigue).

articles.title: Violette Dorange forced to withdraw
articles.excerpt: Following the collision on November 1st off the coast of Bréhat, Violette Dorange and her team did everything possible to get Initiatives-Cœur underway again. Extensive investigations carried out in Lorient revealed more significant structural damage than that observed during the stopover in Roscoff. The time required for repairs will prevent Violette from resuming the race.

articles.title: Bowsprit broken off on 11th Hour racing
articles.excerpt: After making a strong start to the first five days of her first Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe race of Italian-American skipper Francesca Clapcich (11th Hour Racing) looks set to be compromised by the loss last night of the bowsprit of her IMOCA.

articles.title: no respite on the atlantic battleground
articles.excerpt: Il y a ceux qui voudraient plus de vent, ceux qui en ont largement assez et ceux qui aimeraient simplement que la mer leur fiche la paix. Cinq jours après le départ de Saint-Malo, l'Atlantique propose un menu dont personne n'a choisi les plats. Dépression tropicale près des Antilles, grosse marmite météorologique autour des Açores, alizés qui brillent par leur absence : les six catégories de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe évoluent dans des mondes bien différents.

articles.title: Boris Herrmann: “Catching up with Corentin? Never say never”
articles.excerpt: In the IMOCA class, Corentin Horeau (MACSF) still leads the pack. Behind him, Boris Herrmann (Malizia 4) made a significant leap, climbing back into second place. It was a tough battle with Francesca Clapcich (11th Hour Racing) and Sam Goodchild (MACIF Santé Prévoyance), as well as against the elements. He gave his report today.
